# Anuruddha Sutta (MN 127 (PTS MN iii 144))

**ID:** MN 127 (PTS MN iii 144)  
**Section:** Majjhimanikāya (mn)  
**Collection:** Sutta  
**Title (Pali):** Anuruddha Sutta  
**Title (English, from literature):** With Anuruddha  
**PTS:** MN iii 144  
**tipitaka.org (CST):** [https://tipitaka.org/romn/cscd/s0203m.mul2.xml](https://tipitaka.org/romn/cscd/s0203m.mul2.xml)

## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and catalog data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

The *Anuruddha Sutta* (MN 127, PTS MN iii 144) is the 127th discourse of the *Majjhimanikāya* [Humphreys 1956; Ñāṇamoli & Bodhi 1995]. The sutta is set on an occasion when the carpenter Pañcakaṅga invites a group of monks to a meal in order to ask them a doctrinal question [Klaus & Hartmann 2007]. Pañcakaṅga experiences confusion when encouraged to develop the "limitless" (or immeasurable) and "expansive" (or exalted) deliverances of mind, and asks Venerable Anuruddha to explain whether the two states are identical in meaning and differ only in phrasing, or whether they are distinct in both meaning and phrasing [Humphreys 1956]. Anuruddha clarifies that they are different: the immeasurable deliverance of mind (*appamāṇā cetovimutti*) pertains to the radiation of the four divine abodes (*brahmavihāra*s), whereas the exalted deliverance of mind (*mahaggatā cetovimutti*) arises from *kasiṇa* meditation [Rogell 2003; Anālayo 2006]. In this context, "exalted" (*mahaggata*) designates the capacity to spatially pervade a broad area with one's meditation object, and Anuruddha further explains the corresponding heavenly rebirths that can be attained through each practice [Rogell 2003; Anālayo 2006].

Modern scholars note the sutta's definition of *mahaggata* as foundational for understanding commentarial glosses on the contemplation of mental states in *satipaṭṭhāna* meditation [Anālayo 2006].
